instructions: Put the 1.5 lbs baby potatoes in a pot, halving any bigger than a golf ball. Cover them with cold water by 1 inch, add 1 tsp of the salt and bring to a boil. Turn the heat down to a steady simmer and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Meanwhile, mince the 3 shallots. Cut 7 tbsp of the butter into small cubes and put them in the fridge so they stay cold.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels and cut it into 4 portions. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper over both sides.
Put the shallots, the 3 tbsp wine and the 3 tbsp vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat. Boil for 4 to 5 minutes, until only about 1 tbsp of liquid is left. Take it off the heat.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and add the oil. Lay in the cod and cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and lets go of the pan.

Flip the cod, add 1 tbsp of the remaining butter to the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the fish flakes when you press it with a fork. You're cooking it to 145°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. Transfer the cod to a warm plate and cover it with foil.

Set the saucepan with the shallots over the lowest heat. Add 2 cubes of the cold butter and whisk until they melt. Keep adding the butter, a couple of cubes at a time, whisking after each, for about 3 minutes, until the sauce is pale, thick and coats a spoon. Don't let it bubble. If the pan feels hot to the touch, lift it off the heat and keep whisking.
Whisk in 1/4 tsp of the salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Drain the potatoes and toss them with the last 1 tbsp butter and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Spoon the sauce over the cod. Serve with the potatoes.
method_notes: Jardiner Malin (the lead, shown at 4.9 with no count) reduces shallots with white wine and white wine vinegar until about a spoonful is left, then whisks in cold butter bit by bit over very low heat, and serves it with cod. Rouxbe (5.0 from 5 ratings) reduces the shallots and wine by two thirds and keeps the sauce warm, not hot, so it doesn't split; TheYumYumClub pan fries the cod and sauces it the same way. No version has 20 ratings. This follows the lead's sauce ratios, sears the cod in a pan as Rouxbe and TheYumYumClub do rather than baking it, and serves it with boiled potatoes, which the sources leave to the cook.
